approach: issue #380 reports the improve-skill validate engine treating top-level user-invocable: false as the classifier for a by-name skill, which forces a description rewrite that breaks a hidden-but-situational skill's trigger

explore established the conflation is doctrinal, not just mechanical: ADR-0013 deliberately required a DUAL marker (the frontmatter flag AND a description prefix) and was never updated when the prefix spelling drifted from 'Internal skill:' to 'Partial Skill:' across 52 skills

owner reframed the taxonomy in-session: 'partial' (cannot run alone) is documentation with no mechanical consequence, while 'name-only' (must be addressed by name) carries the real rule — its description is kept minimal because the description is the only surface a spurious match can grab

chosen shape is the minimal description AS the enforcement rather than a label for it: description is exactly the marker, identity moves to body and README; classification becomes a string comparison and needs no harness field support
doctrine landed first (governance, ADR-0031 superseding ADR-0013's dual marker, prose mirrors), then the engine, corpus migration, and the three affected suites

why: Owner granted live in-session across two rounds. Round 1 covered improve-skill.feature after being shown that the CR rewrites its classifier scenario and that the two prefix-check scenarios go vacuous once the marker is the classifier. Round 2 extended the grant after a sweep found the same frozen doctrine in two further suites the first grant did not name — the owner was shown the per-suite hit counts and chose 'one CR' over splitting into follow-ups, on the grounds that splitting would leave a window where define-skill instructs authors to write a prefix improve-skill no longer honors. Grant covers REWRITING frozen scenarios that assert the old classifier or the old description prefix in all three suites. Scope note recorded rather than assumed: define-governance.feature's scenario asserting a governance sets user-invocable to false SURVIVES UNCHANGED — visibility remains correct for a governance bar, and only the selection claim moves. Additive scenarios covering the new hidden-but-situational case self-clear and are not claimed under this grant.

title: the adoption template emits the path-read the skill's own earlier section calls a fallback
note: SKILL.md's 'keep the content in a skill' section says reading an agent file by path is brittle, breaks under plugin distribution, and is acceptable only when no skill placement is available. The Adoption template then emits exactly that path-read unconditionally, with no pointer to the preferred skills-preload route. The generator ships the shape its own earlier section deprecates, and it propagates to every adoption command ever generated. Not a scenario failure — a frozen scenario freezes the path-read — so correcting it means moving that scenario, not just the template. Found by the cold impl-judge on the gateway delta.

title: two subject sections on this branch are governed by no scenario
note: Commit 6b24cf71 added 'First: confirm an agent definition is the right artifact' and 'Keep the content in a skill' to define-agent's SKILL.md, and the frozen suite governs neither. Ungraded subject behavior — a revision could drop either silently. Found by the cold impl-judge while checking the gateway delta for regressions; outside that delta's scope, so reported rather than graded.

title: the no-scaffold-before-the-answer rule rides on one word
note: The scenario 'the command shape is settled by where the agent's output goes' passes its second half on the bolded 'first' inside a sentence whose main clause is 'Write a second file'. What actually prevents premature scaffolding is that no default template exists — both live under headings conditioned on the answer. If a later edit adds an 'if unsure, use Adoption' default, the half silently regresses while the text still reads as compliant. Harden the prose so the guard does not depend on an absence.
